Health expenditure, income and population health: a country-year panel

Source: R/data-healthspend.R
healthspend.Rd

A real public panel of 193 countries observed every year from 2000 to 2022 (23 years), assembled from the World Bank World Development Indicators (WDI). It links current health expenditure (from the WHO Global Health Expenditure Database, as redistributed in WDI), its financing mix (out-of-pocket and domestic government shares), real income, population ageing, life expectancy and under-5 mortality. The panel is balanced in its rows (every country has all 23 years) but unbalanced in its values: some country-years are missing (NA) for some indicators, so fitted models use an unbalanced panel. Countries with no health expenditure data in any year (mostly small territories) and all regional and income aggregates are excluded. The build script, with the download calls and the validation checks, is data-raw/healthspend.R in the package's GitHub repository.

Usage

healthspend

Format

A data frame with 4,439 rows (193 countries x 23 years) and 15 columns. The panel index pair is (iso3c, year).

iso3c

factor, ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code (193 levels); the panel individual index

year

integer calendar year, 2000-2022; the panel time index

country

character, World Bank country name

region

factor, World Bank region (7 levels: East Asia & Pacific; Europe & Central Asia; Latin America & Caribbean; Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan & Pakistan; North America; South Asia; Sub-Saharan Africa); time invariant

income

factor, World Bank income group with levels low, lowermiddle, uppermiddle, high; the classification current at download (2026-11-01), so it is time invariant here and does not track past reclassifications

chepc

numeric, current health expenditure (CHE) per capita, PPP, current international dollars (WDI SH.XPD.CHEX.PP.CD), 2 decimals

chereal

numeric, real CHE per capita in constant 2021 international dollars, derived as chegdp / 100 * gdppc; use this (not chepc, which is in current prices) together with gdppc for income elasticities

chegdp

numeric, CHE as a percentage of GDP (SH.XPD.CHEX.GD.ZS)

oop

numeric, out-of-pocket expenditure as a percentage of CHE (SH.XPD.OOPC.CH.ZS), 0-100; divide by 100 for a proportion

gghe

numeric, domestic general government health expenditure as a percentage of CHE (SH.XPD.GHED.CH.ZS), 0-100

gdppc

numeric, GDP per capita, PPP, constant 2021 international dollars (NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.KD), 1 decimal

lifeexp

numeric, life expectancy at birth, total, years (SP.DYN.LE00.IN); period estimates include crisis years, e.g. 14.7 for the Central African Republic in 2009

u5mr

numeric, under-5 mortality rate per 1,000 live births (SH.DYN.MORT)

pop

integer, total population (SP.POP.TOTL)

pop65

numeric, population aged 65 and above, percentage of total (SP.POP.65UP.TO.ZS)

Missing values: chepc 92, chereal 217, chegdp, oop and gghe 91, gdppc 174, u5mr 23; lifeexp, pop and pop65 are complete.

Source

World Bank, World Development Indicators, API v2 (https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/all/indicator/SH.XPD.CHEX.PP.CD?date=2000:2023&format=json&per_page=20000 and the same call for the other indicator codes; country metadata from https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country?format=json&per_page=400), WDI release last updated 2026-10-08, downloaded 2026-11-01. Health expenditure series: World Health Organization, Global Health Expenditure Database (update of 12 December 2025), via WDI. Life expectancy and population: UN World Population Prospects; under-5 mortality: UN Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation; GDP: World Bank International Comparison Program; all via WDI.

Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0). The WDI catalog entry (https://datatopics.worldbank.org/world-development-indicators/) states "This dataset is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0", and the metadata of each of the nine series used carries License_Type "CC BY-4.0". Attribution: "World Bank, World Development Indicators (CC BY 4.0)". Changes from the source: country subset, renamed columns, rounding, and the derived column chereal.

Teaching use

The panel is suited to the classic macro health-economics questions. Take logs first, e.g. hs <- transform(healthspend, lche = log(chereal), lgdp = log(gdppc)).

  • Is health care a luxury good? Income elasticity of real health spending, lche ~ lgdp: pooled vs between vs within vs random effects (panglm() with model = "pooling", "between", "within", "random"), correlated random effects (cre = TRUE) and panhausman() (classical and Mundlak). Year effects (effect = "twoways") remove common shocks and lower the within elasticity from about 1.15 to about 0.84.

  • How persistent is health spending, and what is the long-run income elasticity? Dynamic model with a lagged dependent variable, pangmm() (difference GMM "d" and system GMM "ld", with collapse = TRUE to keep the instrument count below the number of countries); long-run elasticity = b / (1 - rho).

  • What do time-invariant characteristics add once income is allowed to be correlated with the country effect? Hausman-Taylor with income endogenous and population ageing plus region exogenous: paniv(..., model = "hausmantaylor").

  • Does out-of-pocket financing fall as countries grow richer? The out-of-pocket share oop / 100 is a proportion in (0, 1): panglm(family = "beta"), pooled with clustered standard errors or random effects with cre = TRUE.

  • Does the income elasticity differ across countries or across the spending distribution? Random slopes (random = ~ lgdp, with lgdp centred) and fixed-effects quantile regression (panqr(), "mmqr" or "canay").

  • Does spending buy health? Life expectancy or under-5 mortality on lche and lgdp with two-way fixed effects (descriptive: spending is endogenous to health needs).

References

World Bank (2026). World Development Indicators. Washington, DC: The World Bank. https://datatopics.worldbank.org/world-development-indicators/

World Health Organization (2025). Global Health Expenditure Database. https://apps.who.int/nha/database

Getzen, T. E. (2000). Health care is an individual necessity and a national luxury: applying multilevel decision models to the analysis of health care expenditures. Journal of Health Economics, 19(2), 259-270.

Baltagi, B. H. and Moscone, F. (2010). Health care expenditure and income in the OECD reconsidered: evidence from panel data. Economic Modelling, 27(4), 804-811.

Hausman, J. A. and Taylor, W. E. (1981). Panel data and unobservable individual effects. Econometrica, 49(6), 1377-1398.

Examples

data(healthspend)
hs <- transform(healthspend, lche = log(chereal), lgdp = log(gdppc))
ix <- c("iso3c", "year")

## income elasticity of real health spending
fe <- panglm(lche ~ lgdp, data = hs, index = ix, model = "within")
re <- panglm(lche ~ lgdp, data = hs, index = ix, model = "random")
fe2 <- panglm(lche ~ lgdp, data = hs, index = ix, model = "within",
              effect = "twoways", vcov = "cluster")
cbind(within = coef(fe), random = coef(re)[-1], twoways = coef(fe2))
#>       within   random   twoways
#> lgdp 1.14926 1.135463 0.8396004
panhausman(fe, re)
#> 
#> 	Hausman specification test (fixed vs. random effects)
#> 
#> chisq = 3.735, df = 1, p-value = 0.05329
#> alternative hypothesis: one model is inconsistent
#> 
panhausman(fe, method = "mundlak", data = hs)
#> 
#> 	Mundlak specification test (fixed vs. random effects), vcov: cluster
#> 
#> F = 1.463, df = 1, 185, p-value = 0.228
#> Wald chisq = 1.463, df = 1, p-value = 0.2264
#> alternative hypothesis: one model is inconsistent
#> 

## persistence and long-run elasticity: system GMM, collapsed instruments
gs <- pangmm(lche ~ lag(lche, 1) + lgdp | lag(lche, 2:99) + lag(lgdp, 2:99),
             data = hs, index = ix, transformation = "ld",
             model = "twostep", collapse = TRUE)
summary(gs)
#> 
#> Call:
#> pangmm(formula = lche ~ lag(lche, 1) + lgdp | lag(lche, 2:99) + 
#>     lag(lgdp, 2:99), data = hs, index = ix, transformation = "ld", 
#>     model = "twostep", collapse = TRUE)
#> 
#> Estimator: two-way two-step system GMM (Blundell-Bond) 
#> n = 7886  groups = 193  T = 23  instruments = 66 
#> vcov: robust (Windmeijer) 
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>              Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> lag(lche, 1)  0.79999    0.06043  13.238   <2e-16 ***
#> lgdp          0.15476    0.09996   1.548    0.122    
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Arellano-Bond AR(1) test: z = -11.51, p = < 2.2e-16
#> Arellano-Bond AR(2) test: z = 0.418, p = 0.676
#> Sargan test (not robust): chi2(42) = 161.4, p = 6.752e-16
#> Hansen J test (robust): chi2(42) = 65.94, p = 0.0106
#> Wald test for coefficients: chi2(2) = 365, p = < 2.2e-16
#> 
b <- coef(gs)
b[["lgdp"]] / (1 - b[["lag(lche, 1)"]])   # long-run income elasticity
#> [1] 0.7737543

## Hausman-Taylor: income endogenous; ageing and region exogenous
ht <- paniv(lche ~ lgdp + pop65 + region | pop65 + region,
            data = hs, index = ix, model = "hausmantaylor")
coef(ht)
#>                                             (Intercept) 
#>                                            -3.380823494 
#>                                                    lgdp 
#>                                             1.019289147 
#>                                                   pop65 
#>                                             0.043322428 
#>                             regionEurope & Central Asia 
#>                                            -0.080872877 
#>                         regionLatin America & Caribbean 
#>                                             0.047087247 
#> regionMiddle East, North Africa, Afghanistan & Pakistan 
#>                                            -0.051324970 
#>                                     regionNorth America 
#>                                             0.477931406 
#>                                        regionSouth Asia 
#>                                            -0.245957148 
#>                                regionSub-Saharan Africa 
#>                                             0.002156185 

## out-of-pocket share, a proportion: beta regression
hs$oopshare <- hs$oop / 100
bp <- panglm(oopshare ~ lgdp + pop65, data = hs, index = ix,
             model = "pooling", family = "beta", vcov = "cluster")
coef(bp)
#>   (Intercept)          lgdp         pop65 
#>  1.041328e+00 -1.844259e-01 -3.140689e-05 

## quantile heterogeneity of the elasticity
coef(panqr(lche ~ lgdp, data = hs, index = ix, tau = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9),
           model = "mmqr"))
#>       tau=0.1  tau=0.5  tau=0.9
#> lgdp 1.179659 1.149445 1.118256

# \donttest{
## random-effects beta with Mundlak terms, every fifth year (slower)
hs5 <- subset(hs, year %% 5 == 0)
br <- panglm(oopshare ~ lgdp + pop65, data = hs5, index = ix,
             model = "random", family = "beta", cre = TRUE,
             vcov = "cluster", R = 7)
summary(br)
#> 
#> Call:
#> panglm(formula = oopshare ~ lgdp + pop65, data = hs5, index = ix, 
#>     model = "random", family = "beta", vcov = "cluster", cre = TRUE, 
#>     R = 7)
#> 
#> Family: beta  Link: logit  Model: random  Effect: individual 
#> n = 916  groups = 186  vcov: cluster 
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)  1.77971    0.68937   2.582 0.009833 ** 
#> lgdp        -0.19501    0.10056  -1.939 0.052476 .  
#> pop65       -0.04780    0.01323  -3.613 0.000302 ***
#> mean_lgdp   -0.08168    0.12642  -0.646 0.518236    
#> mean_pop65   0.04828    0.01724   2.801 0.005101 ** 
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Log-likelihood: 911.1 
#> Dispersion parameter: 0.02356 
#> Random-intercept SD: 0.9156 
#> Mundlak test (individual means jointly zero, Wald, vcov: cluster): chi2(2) = 8.734, p = 0.01269
#> Residual df: 909  Iterations: 83
#> 

## country-specific income slopes (centre the regressor first)
hs$lgdpc <- hs$lgdp - 9
rs <- panglm(lche ~ lgdpc, data = hs, index = ix, model = "random",
             random = ~ lgdpc, R = 7)
summary(rs)
#> 
#> Call:
#> panglm(formula = lche ~ lgdpc, data = hs, index = ix, model = "random", 
#>     random = ~lgdpc, R = 7)
